title: The Spirit's descent and the two fires of Christ's baptism
english: The Spirit also comes down upon the apostles. For the Spirit is God, and God is a consuming fire (Deuteronomy 4:24). This is why Christ is said to baptize with fire (Luke 3:16): because he poured out the grace of Christ upon his holy disciples in the form of fiery tongues (Acts 2:3), or because of the punishing nature of the fire to come. That final baptism is not saving, but destructive of evil—for no longer will evil and sin hold sway—yet it punishes endlessly.

added_allusions.reason: The clause God is a consuming fire reproduces pyr katanaliskon, the wording of Deuteronomy 4:24 (God is a consuming fire).
Christ is said to baptize with fire reproduces Luke 3:16, he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire (pyri in the Greek of the fragment, matching Luke's en pneumati hagio kai pyri).
Poured out on the holy disciples in the form of fiery tongues (Greek en eidei pyrinon glotton) closely echoes Acts 2:3, tongues as of fire (glossai hosei pyros).
